standard.title: Initiate and sustain exchanges
standard.description: initiate and sustain exchanges, related to students' experiences and perspectives
standard.prior_knowledge: Students entering the background language learner pathway at Y7-8 bring significant home and community experience of the target language — spoken fluency in familiar registers, cultural knowledge, and informal literacy to varying degrees. They have not yet participated in structured academic exchanges, used the target language for sustained opinion-based discussion, or navigated formal and digital interaction contexts in an academic setting.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students initiate and sustain exchanges related to their experiences and perspectives, using culturally appropriate language across face-to-face and digital contexts, sharing opinions and responding to others.

nodes.label: Culturally appropriate initiation and response
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can initiate and sustain exchanges in culturally appropriate ways — including expressing preferences, justifying views, and ensuring others are included.
nodes.minimum_width: Initiate at least one exchange using culturally appropriate conventions and sustain it for at least four turns, including at least one expression of preference or opinion.
nodes.typical_width: Initiate and sustain conversations about personal interests, hobbies and future plans using culturally appropriate conventions; express preferences with reasons; ensure other participants are included; respond to class discussion questions with agreement or disagreement; clarify or paraphrase teacher instructions when needed.
wider: Compare culturally appropriate conversation initiation and participation conventions in the target language with Australian English — identify specific differences in how inclusion, agreement and disagreement are managed
Reflect on own home language interaction patterns — identify where school target language interaction differs from home use and discuss what adjustments are needed
nodes.hinge_reason: Culturally appropriate initiation is the prerequisite for all sustained academic interaction. Students who rely on home register conventions without adjustment cannot participate effectively in structured school-context exchanges.

response_modes.reason: Entry pathway students need to build a reliable school-context interaction register through repeated practice. Regular structured exchanges — peer discussions, class debates, digital interactions — consolidate culturally appropriate conventions before students can deploy them flexibly.

success_criteria: Initiates an exchange using culturally appropriate conventions
Sustains the exchange for at least four turns including at least one opinion or preference expression

nodes.label: Digital and written interaction
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can exchange information and share experiences through digital and written formats — emails, online journals, blogs — using appropriate format conventions.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least one digital or written interaction text (email, journal entry, or blog post) using appropriate target language conventions for the format.
nodes.typical_width: Exchange emails about school, home and social activities using appropriate format; maintain contact with peers through digital platforms; keep a secure online journal documenting highlights of daily life; exchange information about special events and community celebrations.
wider: Compare email and digital interaction conventions in the target language with English equivalents — identify differences in greeting, register, sign-off and structural conventions
Create a bilingual digital interaction text for a dual-language audience — selecting language for each section based on audience and purpose

response_modes.reason: Digital and written interaction conventions vary across format types — email, blog, journal, social media. Practising across varied digital formats builds the flexible written interaction capacity the descriptor requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background language learner entry students often use the target language in digital contexts outside school. Width investment here connects school learning to authentic digital practice — activating existing habits while building formal register awareness.
success_criteria: Produces a digital or written interaction text using appropriate format conventions
Uses register appropriate to the format and intended recipient

nodes.label: Responding to invitations and social scenarios
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can respond to invitations and participate in exchanges about special events and community celebrations using appropriate social language.
nodes.minimum_width: Respond appropriately to at least one invitation — accepting or declining — using appropriate target language conventions, and exchange information about at least one special event or celebration.
nodes.typical_width: Respond to invitations — accepting and declining in appropriate ways; share information about special events and community celebrations; participate in exchanges about personal and community life with peers in target language communities; share life experiences in face-to-face and online contexts.
wider: Compare invitation and response conventions across different target language community contexts — identify how formality and register vary depending on relationship and occasion
Create and respond to an invitation for a culturally significant event — demonstrating full command of the relevant social language conventions

response_modes.reason: Social scenario response integrates culturally appropriate interaction (node 1) and digital interaction skills (node 2) into the full range of social communication contexts. The teaching investment is in creating genuine social scenarios — real invitations, real events — that require authentic target language use.

success_criteria: Responds to an invitation using appropriate acceptance or decline conventions
Exchanges information about a special event or celebration in culturally appropriate target language
